title: AudioTranscript: cutting audio at the silences

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How do you turn a long recording into text when a recognition service only wants small pieces?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes, but where you cut matters. AudioTranscript takes a WAV file and finds the silences. It breaks the recording into chunks around those quiet moments, so it doesn't slice through the middle of a word.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Each chunk goes to a speech recognition service, and the pieces of text come back and are joined into one transcript. The current version uses Amazon's recognition service.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Small and focused. It's pure Python, MIT licensed, and Antoine's note describes it as an audio ingestion and transcription pipeline with timestamp alignment.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So the idea is one clean pipeline.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Right: split at silence, recognize, stitch back together. The written page has the details.
